newsitem.title: USA: Johnston stops dividend in Q3, thereafter.
newsitem.headline: Johnston stops dividend in Q3, thereafter.

text.p: Johnston Industries Inc said on Wednesday that it will pay no dividend in the third quarter or in subsequent quarters.
The company said in a news release that the dividend issue would be reviewed on a quarterly basis, as the effect of its restructuring plan is felt.
Johnston said its restructuring plan will generate "substantial profitability" over time, but the effect will not be felt until after the third quarter of 1997.
Johnston reported a second quarter loss of $0.63 per share, including a restructuring charge, compared with a profit of $0.21 per share for the same period a year ago.

The company said that shutting its Langdale plant in Valley, Ala., will eliminate $2 million in annual losses and cut its annual payroll by $14 million to $15 million while having only a limited impact on revenues.
Johnston said its capital spending budget for 1998 is $20 million, double the current year's budget.
Johnston makes multiaxial, non-crimp reinforcing fabrics used to reinforce plastics for a variety of markets and applications.
